title: The Last Fire
tagline: He burned Quito rather than let it fall — a warrior's final act.

scenes.text: The Inca Empire, 1533. The Spanish have captured Atahualpa, collected his ransom in gold — and strangled him anyway. Rumiñahui, the greatest Inca general, will not wait to be next.
He races south to Quito — the northern capital — arriving before the Spanish. He buries Atahualpa's gold treasure so the conquerers will never find it. Some believe it has never been found.

challenge.instruction: Before the Spanish can reach Quito, Rumiñahui's cord keepers must count what is to be hidden. Read only the cords of the colour asked — yellow for gold, red for warriors — and give him the total.
challenge.fact: Rumiñahui ('Stone Eye') was Atahualpa's most capable general. When Pizarro captured and executed the Inca emperor in 1533, Rumiñahui gathered the northern army and led resistance from Quito. Rather than let Pizarro's forces loot the city's treasures, he burned Quito and hid its gold — a legendary hoard that has never been found.

scenes.text: When Sebastián de Belalcázar approaches with a Spanish force and thousands of native allies, Rumiñahui employs Inca guerrilla tactics — ambushes in mountain passes, scorched crops, scattered forces.

challenge.instruction: Belalcázar's horsemen are coming up the road. Rumiñahui's warriors have hidden pits across the plain — bring your own men through without falling into one.
challenge.fact: Belalcázar marched on Quito in 1534 with about 200 Spaniards and thousands of Cañari and other native allies who hated Atahualpa's rule. Rumiñahui fought them at Teocajas and in the passes for months before falling back on the city.

scenes.text: He cannot win in open battle — Spanish steel, horses, and guns are decisive. But he refuses to surrender. He burns Quito to the ground rather than let it become a Spanish trophy.

challenge.instruction: Quito will burn rather than become a Spanish trophy — but first its treasure must go. Lead the llama train to each load before the Spanish arrive, then on into the mountains.
challenge.fact: The lost treasure of Quito became one of the great legends of the Americas. Expeditions searched for it for centuries, and legends of El Dorado were partly inspired by the belief that Rumiñahui had hidden an incomprehensible fortune somewhere in the Andes. No credible discovery has ever been made.

scenes.text: Captured after a volcanic eruption disrupts his forces, he is tortured to reveal the treasure's location. He says nothing. His silence is the last act of resistance.

challenge.instruction: The Spanish close in from every side. Rumiñahui's bands fall back through the gorges, cutting each rope bridge behind them — find the line of retreat that crosses every bridge exactly once.
challenge.fact: The Spanish advantage in the Inca conquest was not just steel and gunpowder — it was horses. The Inca had no large domesticated animals. The sight of mounted soldiers, armored in steel, was psychologically devastating. Rumiñahui understood this and consistently drew Spanish forces into terrain that negated the horse — steep trails, forest, and fast rivers.

scenes.text: Rumiñahui is executed in Quito in 1535. Today he is a national hero of Ecuador — a symbol of indigenous resistance, of a world that burned rather than submitted.

challenge.instruction: Rumiñahui is gone, but the roads he fought along remain. Run the message through every post of the Inca road and home again, as the chasquis did.
challenge.fact: The Qhapaq Ñan, the Inca road network of some 30,000 km, became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2014, shared by six countries from Colombia to Chile — Ecuador among them.

challenge.instruction: The Spanish will forbid the feast of the Sun and put out its fires. Kindle the last fire as the priests did at Inti Raymi, bringing the light to a single point.
challenge.fact: Rumiñahui was executed in Quito in 1535. Ecuador honours him as a national hero of indigenous resistance, and a canton near Quito bears his name.

scenes.speaker: Rumiñahui
scenes.text: Genoa is under Riot. At the end of every round, any side whose Strength totals under 5 is swept from the board. Francesco Borromini is already there and far too weak to last. Put me there and hold.

challenge.instruction: Fight lesson 4 · Survival. Deploy Rumiñahui to Genoa, keep at least 5 Strength there, and End Turn until two round endings have passed.
challenge.fact: A Local Survival event is a test, not a fight: at the end of each round every side at the location is checked, and a total under 5 loses every card there to the discard pile. Reinforce with followers, or retrieve a weak card before the round ends.
